R0182.title: IoT Data Tampering Attack
R0182.definition: Attackers tamper with data transmitted or stored by IoT devices, leading to incorrect decisions or system failure.
R0182.description: IoT devices collect, transmit, and store large amounts of sensitive data. Without integrity protection, attackers can tamper with data through man-in-the-middle attacks, device intrusion, etc. Typical scenarios include: tampering sensor readings to affect automated decisions (such as temperature, pressure, humidity), modifying device logs to cover attack traces, forging authentication data, tampering control commands, etc. In industrial, medical, and smart city scenarios, this may cause serious consequences.
R0182.influence: Dangerous decisions based on incorrect data, system control failure, attack behavior hidden, audit logs untrustworthy.

references.title: Privacy and Integrity Protection for IoT Multimodal Data Using ...

observables: Sensor-reported data shows systematic deviation from redundant sensors or historical baselines without a reasonable physical cause
Device logs are tampered with or missing records for key time periods, inconsistent with upstream and downstream system data
The transmission link lacks integrity checks, with data packet contents modified in transit
Control commands are tampered with during dispatch, with execution results inconsistent with the command source records
